simpler-osmosis.response:
Osmosis is water moving through a membrane that only water can pass through.

The membrane lets water through but blocks the dissolved stuff (like salt or sugar). If one side has more dissolved stuff, water tends to move from the side with less dissolved stuff to the side with more. It keeps going until the two sides balance out.

A concrete example: put a saltwater solution on one side of such a membrane and plain water on the other. Water will slowly cross into the saltwater side, diluting it, until the concentrations even out.

The one condition to keep in mind: this only happens when the membrane is selectively permeable — it has to let water through while blocking the solute. If the membrane lets everything through, you just get ordinary mixing, not osmosis.
